title: I Was Hired to Clean a Moving Truck After an Accident. Then I Found a Row of Children's Height Marks Inside the Cargo Area (PART 2)

blocks.text: The height marks weren't for fun. They were how the people running the truck sorted children by age and size before handing them over.

Federal investigators identified the network within days. It moved unaccompanied migrant children who'd crossed the border alone, often fleeing violence in Central America. Many were released by authorities to adults claiming to be relatives or "sponsors." This network supplied fake sponsors. Then it moved the children in the truck to farms and meatpacking plants in three states, where they were forced to work long shifts to "repay" their travel debts.

The little girl named beside the final mark was Ana, twelve. She'd run away from a shelter in Texas two days before the accident after a man claiming to be her uncle visited. She was reported missing that morning.
The network had planned to deliver her to a "sponsor" in Tulsa the next day.
Using the names on the wall, investigators traced the truck's routes and found Ana that night at a house outside Oklahoma City, waiting to be moved. She was frightened but unhurt.

Over the next year, agents located twenty-one of the twenty-six children whose names were on that wall. They'd been working on a poultry farm, at a car wash, and at a meat processing plant. All were placed in protective care. Nine people were charged with child labor trafficking.
The driver who fled the accident was caught in Arkansas.
Ana's real aunt, who lives in Houston and had been trying to sponsor her legally for months, was granted custody that spring.
I kept cleaning trucks. I just look harder now.
If you suspect human trafficking or child labor, call the National Human Trafficking Hotline at 1-888-373-7888.
